texts.li: {A_nameDef} found the {THING} in the stockpile gone soft and grey, and had to step outside for a breath.
{A_nameDef} went for {THING} to cook with and came back empty-handed. The whole stack had turned.
The smell of rotten {THING} met {A_nameDef} at the storeroom door.
{A_nameDef} counted what was left of the {THING} that hadn't spoiled. It didn't take long.
{A_nameDef} picked up some of the {THING}, sniffed it once, and threw it on the rot pile.
[summer|hot] Flies had found the {THING} in the stores before {A_nameDef} did.
{A_nameDef} said what everyone was thinking: the {THING} should have been eaten a week ago.
{A_nameDef} worked on in the rain, shirt stuck flat to {A_possessive} back.
Rain ran off {A_nameDef}'s hair and down inside {A_possessive} collar. Nobody had thought to make {A_objective} a coat.
{A_nameDef} wrung out {A_possessive} sleeves at the end of the job and got about a cup of water from each.
{A_nameDef} squelched with every step and gave up trying to stay dry.
{A_nameDef} watched someone go by in a good coat and kept working in the downpour.
[child] {A_nameDef} came in dripping and stood by the fire until the floor around {A_objective} was a puddle.
{A_nameDef} woke up face to face with the {THING} someone had left in {A_possessive} room.
{A_nameDef} stubbed a toe on the {THING} by the bed, for the second time.
{A_nameDef} asked, not for the first time, who had dumped a {THING} in {A_possessive} bedroom.
{A_nameDef} lay in bed looking at the {THING} in the corner and wondered when it would be moved.
[morning] The first thing {A_nameDef} saw that morning was the {THING} on the floor.
[child] {A_nameDef} built a fort around the {THING} in {A_possessive} room, because nobody was taking it away.
